readerValues.programmeDescription: Cybersecurity & Cybercrime at Leiden combines computing, governance, law and criminology to study digital security and crime. Students examine how networked systems work, how attacks occur, who commits and experiences cybercrime, and how organisations and public institutions can respond. Research methods, academic skills and multidisciplinary projects connect these perspectives.
readerValues.comparisonExplanation: No close UCR comparison was found for the documented curriculum. UCR has genuine strengths in computing, law, misinformation, digital ethics and organizational study. Its strongest combinations do not sustain Leiden’s integrated study of cyber threats, crime, protection and response. The unpublished required third-year study remains separate from this academic judgment.

curriculum.limitation: The listed components total 150 EC: 120 EC of compulsory study in the first two years and 30 EC of third-year elective space. The remaining 30 EC of compulsory third-year study, including the final project, still require confirmation. This is an incomplete curriculum, not a certified 180-EC degree plan.

componentNotes.y1-skills-1: The skills labs develop academic and professional skills in small groups. Attendance and assessment requirements apply.
componentNotes.y1-project: A 10-EC multidisciplinary project on online deception and disinformation. Its credits are counted once within the first year.
componentNotes.y2-defence: Builds on the study of cyber attacks, moving from vulnerabilities to access controls, defensive measures and organisational security.
componentNotes.y2-project: A 10-EC multidisciplinary ransomware project, counted within the second year. Attendance and individual assessment requirements apply.
componentNotes.y3-open-elective-space: 30 EC for electives, a minor or approved study or internship options. Level, approval and non-overlap rules apply. Honours courses and specified overlapping minors and courses cannot be used here.

comparisonScope.assessed: The 23 documented components totaling 150 EC: 120 EC of first- and second-year compulsory study and 30 EC of genuine open study. The confirmed technical, criminological, legal, governance and integration teaching informs the judgment.
comparisonScope.excluded: The remaining 30 EC of required third-year study, individual final-project weight and assessment/access requirements, and full degree progression. The documented subset is not a certified complete 180-EC degree plan.

finding: Reader sees genuine UCR strengths and the subject-specific cyber integration shortfall, with documented versus nominal credits and unpublished required final-year study clearly separated. Open study is not missing required study. No professional-role, title, language or exact assessment-format veto.
